triage.verifier_justification: The pre-fix module was an explicitly declared stub: its header carried a `deferred_outputs` block naming all six operative outputs (floor_duty_applies, the two exception judgments, and the general/special/column-2 rate outputs) with stated deferral reasons (sibling-name collision, or dependence on a deferred output), so the module formally never claimed to encode the below-threshold scope, the heading exceptions, or the 15% column-1 replacement rates. The only meaning it did encode — the `reciprocal_south_korea_floor_duty_rate` parameter — survives the fix byte-identical in value (`formula: '0.15'`) and window (`effective_from: '2026-02-15'`); the only edits to it are a `source:` string and a proof-atom kind/excerpt swap, which the rubric classes as provenance/mechanical. Nothing encoded disagreed with HTS 9903.02.80 (resolved text confirms the 15% rates, the exception headings, and the subdivision (v)(xxiv)(a) scope), and the composition in the same commit imports only "each country heading's rate parameter", so no consumer received a wrong answer from the stub. This is completion of declared-absent coverage inside the same PR that introduced the stub, i.e. new outputs and scope the module never claimed, not a fidelity correction.
triage.verifier_notes:
Counter-argument a reviewer should weigh: the pre-fix `summary` did recite the full provision (exceptions plus the 15% replacement rates) while the module exported nothing operative, so someone reading the summary as a claim could call the gap `unrepresented_clause`. I weight the `deferred_outputs` block higher because it is RuleSpec's formal non-claim marker and it sat in the same header; the deferral reasons are encoder mechanics (name collision with the terminated predecessor's plain exports), not a mis-encoding of source meaning. Commit F2 frames it the same way: "the five floor stub modules are complete encodings" — completion language, not correction language, and the same PR (#1197) both created and completed the stub, so nothing wrong was ever in a merged state.

Two follow-ups that are about the POST-fix content, not the candidate defect, and would need their own cases if the corpus wants them: (1) the source text reads "rate of duty under column 1-General or column 1-Special less than 15 percent" but the new `reciprocal_south_korea_floor_duty_applies` formula conjoins both ("applicable_subheading_general_duty_rate < threshold and applicable_subheading_special_duty_rate < threshold"); the new summary defends this as the complement of sibling 9903.02.79 so the pair partitions without overlap — defensible, but it is an or/and divergence from the literal text worth a reviewer's eye. (2) The pre-fix second proof atom on the rate parameter was `kind: condition` / `excerpt: less than 15 percent` — grounding a 15% rate parameter on the threshold clause; the fix re-grounds it to "Rates of duty (1-Special): 15%". That is a real mis-grounding but excerpt/citation-string only, which the rubric calls mechanical (provenance), and the value never changed.
